name: Factual recall
description: Retrieving a specific fact about the world that is either known or not; little inference required once the fact is available.

name: Expert domain knowledge
description: Specialist knowledge at graduate, professional, or research level (advanced science, law, medicine) that a well-read non-specialist would not have.

name: Deductive/logical reasoning
description: Deriving a conclusion that follows necessarily from given premises — formal logic, validity checking, constraint satisfaction, elimination.

name: Causal reasoning
description: Judging what caused what, counterfactuals, responsibility, or the direction of an effect.

name: Temporal reasoning
description: Reasoning over dates, durations, event ordering, or scheduling.

name: Spatial/geometric reasoning
description: Reasoning over position, direction, shape, rotation, navigation, or geometric relationships.

name: Relational/multi-hop inference
description: Chaining two or more relations or documents together to reach an answer no single fact provides.

name: State tracking
description: Maintaining and updating a mental model of entities, positions, or quantities as a sequence of changes is applied.

name: Commonsense reasoning
description: Everyday physical, social, or practical knowledge that people share implicitly and rarely state.

name: Numerical reasoning
description: Arithmetic and quantitative manipulation — counting, computing, comparing magnitudes, unit handling.

name: Mathematical problem solving
description: Multi-step derivation with formal mathematical technique (algebra, calculus, proof, competition math), beyond plain arithmetic.

name: Symbolic/abstract manipulation
description: Applying formal rules to abstract symbols where the symbols carry no real-world meaning — bracket matching, algebraic structures, formal grammars.

name: Code generation
description: Producing runnable code that satisfies a specification.

name: Code understanding
description: Reading existing code or a technical API to predict behavior, find a bug, or answer a question about it.

name: Reading comprehension (long-context)
description: Locating and combining information from a long supplied document or documents rather than from parametric knowledge.

name: Structured data interpretation
description: Reading a table, chart, schema, or other structured layout and answering from its structure.

name: Linguistic/pragmatic understanding
description: Sensitivity to how language works — ambiguity, word order, sarcasm, register, translation error, wordplay.

name: Information extraction
description: Pulling specific requested content out of supplied source material without transforming it.

name: Instruction/format following
description: Obeying explicit output constraints — length, casing, required or forbidden words, sections, structural format.

name: Stylistic control
description: Writing in a requested tone, voice, persona, or register, as distinct from a structural format rule.

name: Creative/open-ended generation
description: Producing original content with no single correct answer, judged on quality rather than correctness.

name: Multi-turn dialogue coherence
description: Maintaining consistency and carrying context across more than one conversational turn.

name: Truthfulness/calibration
description: Resisting a false premise or popular misconception, and knowing when to decline rather than guess.

name: Evidence evaluation
description: Weighing conflicting, noisy, outdated, or unreliable sources to decide what to believe.

name: Ethical/normative judgment
description: Judging what is permissible, obligatory, legal, or socially appropriate rather than what is factually true.

name: Tool use
description: Invoking an external tool, API, or command and using its result. Expected to be near-absent in this corpus — apply only where a sample genuinely requires it.

name: Planning
description: Devising an ordered multi-step plan of action before executing it. Expected to be near-absent in this corpus — apply only where a sample genuinely requires it.

name: Diagnosis
description: Inferring the underlying cause of a reported fault or symptom from evidence. Expected to be near-absent in this corpus — apply only where a sample genuinely requires it.
